vulnerabilities.description: The fix for CVE-2025-68161 was incomplete: it addressed hostname verification only when enabled via the log4j2.sslVerifyHostName system property, but not when configured through the verifyHostName attribute of the <Ssl> element. Although the verifyHostName configuration attribute was introduced in Log4j Core 2.12.0, it was silently ignored in all versions through 2.25.3, leaving TLS connections vulnerable to interception regardless of the configured value. A network-based attacker may be able to perform a man-in-the-middle attack when all of the following conditions are met: an SMTP, Socket, or Syslog appender is in use; TLS is configured via a nested <Ssl> element; and the attacker can present a certificate issued by a CA trusted by the appender's configured trust store, or by the default Java trust store if none is configured. This issue does not affect users of the HTTP appender. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4j Core 2.25.4, which corrects this issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not configure any Log4j SMTP, Socket or Syslog appender with TLS.

ratings.justification: The flaw only affects TLS connections opened by SMTP, Socket or Syslog appenders. Liquibase Secure configures none of them, so log4j-core never opens a TLS connection.

analysis.detail: Log4j Core ignored the verifyHostName attribute of a nested Ssl element, so TLS host name verification was skipped; fixed in 2.25.4. It matters only when an SMTP, Socket or Syslog appender is configured with a nested Ssl element and an attacker can present a certificate from a trusted CA. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 have no standalone log4j-core. The Databricks JDBC driver inside liquibase-commercial-databricks.jar bundles a copy relocated to com.databricks.client.jdbc42.internal.apache.logging.log4j, whose class set matches 2.20.0, in range. Outside Log4j itself only the driver's bundled Netty logging adapter references it, and the jar carries no Log4j configuration file. From 5.1.0 that copy is gone, and log4j-core is bundled unrelocated in the liquibase-checks extension for the Phileas library: 2.25.3 in 5.1.0 and 5.1.1, in range, then the fixed 2.25.4 in 5.2.0 and 2.26.1 in 5.2.1 through 6.0.0. The build strips Phileas's log4j2.xml from that jar, so log4j-core runs with its built-in default configuration, which writes only to the console. The license-tracking application archived under /liquibase/dist carries only log4j-api with the log4j-to-slf4j bridge and logs through logback. No shipped jar contains a Log4j configuration that declares an SMTP, Socket or Syslog appender, and a source review found no Liquibase code that configures one.
